title: How did Beatrix Potter put real animals into stories?
answer: Beatrix Potter watched real animals closely before drawing animals who wore clothes and had adventures in her stories. She kept rabbits and other small animals when she was young. Her most famous rabbit story began as a letter with pictures for a child. The careful details in the plants and animal bodies make her made-up scenes feel more like places a reader could visit. Potter also cared for farms and land in England’s Lake District.
facts: The Tale of Peter Rabbit was first shared in an illustrated letter.
aliases: why was Peter Rabbit drawn that way

title: Why does Wonderland play with words and rules?
answer: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an English writer who also taught mathematics. In Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, Alice meets characters who give strange answers to ordinary questions. The rules of a game or a conversation can change while she is trying to follow them. Readers may laugh because they recognize how a normal rule works and notice when the story twists it.
facts: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland includes illustrations by John Tenniel in early editions.

title: Why did the Brothers Grimm collect fairy tales?
answer: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected stories in German-speaking Europe and printed versions of many of them. Tales people tell aloud can change a little with each storyteller. Publishing a version lets people read that wording long after the teller is gone. Later tellers and publishers changed details again, so two books may have different versions of the same story. The Grimms were also scholars of words and older writing.
facts: The Grimm collection includes versions of stories now known as Little Red Riding Hood and Hansel and Gretel.

title: Where did the Winnie-the-Pooh characters come from?
answer: English writer A. A. Milne wrote about a boy named Christopher Robin and his animal friends. Milne’s son was also named Christopher Robin. Real stuffed animals from the family helped inspire some of the characters, including the bear and the donkey. The toys tell us something about where the stories began. The characters on the page have their own worries, mistakes, and ways of talking, which are the writer’s inventions.
facts: The New York Public Library keeps several of the original stuffed animals in its collection.

title: Who wrote The Wonderful Wizard of Oz?
answer: L. Frank Baum wrote a story about Dorothy, a girl who travels from Kansas to the made-up Land of Oz. Her companions all hope the Wizard can help them. As they travel, their actions show readers what courage and kindness can look like. The book was illustrated by W. W. Denslow. It came out long before the well-known movie, and some details in the book differ from the movie’s version.
facts: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz was first published in 1900.

title: What helped Louisa May Alcott write Little Women?
answer: Louisa May Alcott grew up with sisters in Massachusetts. She used parts of family life as inspiration when she wrote Little Women, the story of four sisters in a fictional family. One chapter can focus on an ordinary disagreement or a plan to help a neighbor. Those moments show the sisters making choices and learning what matters to them. Readers can compare an author’s life with her fiction without expecting every detail to match.
facts: Alcott and her family lived at the house now called the Wayside for part of her youth.

title: How did a map help start Treasure Island?
answer: Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson made a drawing of an island and used it to imagine a story. In Treasure Island, the map gives characters a reason to travel and a place to search. It also suggests details that can become part of the plot, like a dangerous stretch of shore or a spot someone wants to find first. A map can help a writer keep track of where a character has been and where they might go next.
facts: The novel first appeared as a series of parts before it was published as a book.

title: Why did Jules Verne write about imagined trips?
answer: French writer Jules Verne told stories about journeys across oceans, around the world, and to places nobody could really visit. In one book travelers ride in an imagined submarine. In another they try to circle the world on a tight schedule. Details about machines and places help the reader picture what happens. A writer can start with real facts and then ask what might happen in a world with a different machine or a surprising trip.
facts: Jules Verne’s books include A Journey to the Centre of the Earth.

title: How did Langston Hughes bring music into poetry?
answer: Langston Hughes wrote poetry, plays, and stories about Black life in the United States. He listened to the sounds of blues and jazz and used some of their rhythms and patterns in poems. Reading a Hughes poem aloud can help you hear when words speed up, slow down, or repeat. He was among the writers of the Harlem Renaissance, when artists made and shared new work in and around Harlem.
facts: Hughes published a collection titled The Weary Blues in the 1920s.

title: How did E. B. White make a farm story feel real?
answer: E. B. White wrote Charlotte’s Web, a story about a pig, a spider, and a girl. Some of its animals speak and plan like people, yet they also do things that real animals do. A spider’s work on a web, a barn’s everyday sounds, and the way humans care for animals help ground the story. White wrote essays as well as stories for young readers.
facts: E. B. White also wrote the children’s books Stuart Little and The Trumpet of the Swan.

title: What did Mozart make with music?
answer: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was a composer from Salzburg, in what is now Austria. He began making and playing music when he was very young and traveled with his family to perform. He later wrote for many combinations of musicians. An opera uses music to tell a story onstage, while a concerto gives a featured player a part to play with a larger group. Mozart wrote in both of these forms, as well as many others.
facts: Mozart wrote an early stage work called Apollo and Hyacinth as a child.

title: Why is Louis Armstrong remembered in jazz?
answer: Louis Armstrong grew up in New Orleans and became a celebrated jazz trumpeter and singer. He could take a tune listeners recognized and change the way some notes fell on the beat. Instead of playing only the same version each time, a jazz musician may invent part of the music while performing. Armstrong’s solos and recordings helped people hear what one featured player could do inside a band.
facts: One of Armstrong’s nicknames was Satchmo.

title: How did Ella Fitzgerald use her voice like an instrument?
answer: Ella Fitzgerald was a jazz singer known for the care she took with pitch and rhythm. At times she sang syllables without ordinary words, choosing sounds such as short pulses or long notes. This kind of singing is called scat. It can work like a trumpet or piano solo, where the performer makes musical choices as they go. Fitzgerald could sing familiar tunes in ways that made listeners hear new details.
facts: Ella Fitzgerald was known as the First Lady of Song.

title: How did Duke Ellington write for his band?
answer: Duke Ellington led a jazz orchestra and wrote music it could play. He knew the different voices of the people in his band, so a part for one player could sound different from a part for another on the same kind of instrument. Ellington also worked with other composers, including Billy Strayhorn. A band’s sound comes from what musicians write, how each performer plays, and how the players listen to one another.
facts: Billy Strayhorn wrote Take the “A” Train, which became a famous tune played by Ellington’s orchestra.

title: Why does the Mona Lisa’s face look so softly shaded?
answer: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa as a portrait. Around the eyes and mouth, the changes from light to dark are very gentle. Hard edges would give the face a more sharply drawn look. Farther back, a landscape of rocks and water seems to stretch beyond the person in the chair. Looking from the face to the landscape lets you see two different uses of soft detail in the same painting.
facts: The Louvre in Paris keeps the Mona Lisa.

title: Why did Van Gogh paint several sunflower pictures?
answer: Vincent van Gogh made several paintings of sunflowers in jars and vases. Some use lots of yellow, yet the light and dark yellows still let you pick out the petals, flower heads, and background. The flowers can look lively or dried out depending on which bloom you look at. Comparing two versions helps you see how an artist can change the balance of colors without choosing a completely different subject.
facts: Some of Van Gogh’s sunflower paintings were made while he lived in Arles, in southern France.

title: What did Frida Kahlo put into her self-portraits?
answer: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter who often used herself as the person in a picture. She chose clothes, plants, objects, and settings that help tell the viewer something about her life and the ideas that mattered to her. A painter can see their own appearance in a mirror, but a self-portrait can also include details that a mirror would not show. That is one way an artist can tell a story without using a sentence.
facts: Kahlo’s family home in Mexico City is now a museum often called the Blue House.

title: Why does Hokusai’s Great Wave look so large?
answer: In Hokusai’s print of a great wave off Kanagawa, the dark blue wave curls over boats close to the front of the picture. Japan’s Mount Fuji looks tiny in the background, although a mountain is much bigger than a wave. Those sizes make sense because the boats and breaking wave are shown much nearer to the viewer. The picture was printed from carved blocks, so artists could make more than one copy.
facts: Hokusai’s print is often called The Great Wave.

title: How did Georgia O’Keeffe make small things feel huge?
answer: Georgia O’Keeffe painted flowers, hills, bones, buildings, and other things she looked at closely. In some flower paintings, a small petal fills a large part of the picture. A viewer can study shapes and curves that might usually go unnoticed while passing a flower outside. She also painted scenes from the southwestern United States, where dry hills and wide skies gave her other shapes and colors to look at.
facts: Georgia O’Keeffe spent many years living and working in New Mexico.

title: How can a quilt tell a story?
answer: Artist Faith Ringgold made artworks that brought pictures, words, and fabric together. A story quilt can have a picture in the middle and written pieces around it, with patterned cloth framing what you read and see. You might notice a neighborhood or a person in the image, then read about a moment in that person’s life. Ringgold used cloth as a real part of the storytelling, including its colors, texture, and borders.
facts: Faith Ringgold’s picture book Tar Beach grew out of her story-quilt work.

title: Why did Jacob Lawrence tell one history in many paintings?
answer: Jacob Lawrence painted a series about the movement of many Black Americans from the South to other regions of the United States. One picture can show a train station, another a room, another a group waiting for work. Each painting gives one small part of a longer story. A visitor can use the pictures and their captions to think about the different reasons people moved and what they hoped to find.
facts: The Migration Series has sixty panels.

title: How did Alma Thomas make pictures out of patches of color?
answer: Alma Thomas painted groups of bright marks that can look as if they are moving in rows, rings, or streams. Small spaces between the marks let quieter colors show. She could change the feeling of a picture by changing the order of the colors or the direction the marks seemed to move. Some of her paintings drew ideas from gardens, light, and space without trying to copy a view exactly.
facts: Alma Thomas taught art in Washington, D.C., before devoting more time to her painting.

title: How did M. C. Escher make shapes fit together?
answer: M. C. Escher made prints in which groups of shapes fit together like tiles. He could turn an ordinary outline into something that looks like a fish or another animal and still have the edges fit its neighbors. In some pictures the shapes get smaller and smaller near the edge. The change in size can make a flat design feel as if it goes on farther than the paper does.

title: Which shapes can tile a floor without leaving gaps?
answer: A tessellation covers a flat surface with shapes that fit just up to one another, without gaps or overlaps. Squares can do it because four square corners meet exactly around one point. Equilateral triangles can do it too. Circles lined up in rows leave curved gaps between them, so circles alone cannot cover a floor without overlap. Tile designs can also use several different shapes together.
facts: Three regular hexagons can meet at a point and fill the space around it.

title: What makes a flat shape a polygon?
answer: A polygon is a closed flat shape made by joining straight sides end to end. A triangle is a polygon with three sides. A rectangle has four sides. A circle is flat and closed, but its edge curves, so it is not a polygon. The inside angles and the lengths can change a lot while the shape keeps the same number of sides. That is why two different-looking shapes can still be the same kind of polygon.
facts: An octagon has eight sides, whether or not all those sides are the same length.

title: How do the faces of a box fit together?
answer: A rectangular box has six flat faces. Each face meets its neighbor along an edge, and three edges come together at a corner. A corner of a solid shape is called a vertex. Opposite faces on the box match in size. On a cube, all six faces match and each one is a square. On many other boxes, a top face and a side face have different shapes or sizes.
facts: A rectangular box and a cube each have twelve edges and eight vertices.

title: What makes a can shaped like a cylinder?
answer: A straight circular cylinder has two matching round ends and a curved surface between them. A typical soup can is close to that shape. If you could unroll its side wall onto a table, it would look like a rectangle. One side of that rectangle would be as long as the distance around the round end. The other would measure how tall the can is.
facts: A cylinder like a soup can has two flat circular faces.

title: Why is an ice cream cone shaped like a cone?
answer: A round cone has a circular base and a surface that gets narrower until it reaches a point. An empty ice cream cone is like the hollow side of that solid shape. A can has two circular ends that stay the same size. A cone’s cross sections parallel to its base get smaller and smaller as you move toward the tip. You can see that difference by comparing water levels inside a cone and inside a straight-sided can.
facts: The single tip of a cone is called its apex or vertex.

title: How is a sphere different from a circle?
answer: A circle is flat, like the outline you draw around the bottom of a cup. A sphere is round in every direction, like a smooth ball. The points on a perfect sphere’s surface are all the same distance from its center. If you could slice an orange right through its middle and look at the cut, the outline would be close to a circle. A slice closer to its skin would be smaller.
facts: A perfect sphere has no flat faces, straight edges, or corners.

title: How do you read the hands on a clock?
answer: On many clocks, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand points at the twelve, it is at the start of an hour. Each number farther around counts another five minutes. If the minute hand is at the six, half an hour has passed. The hour hand also moves slowly during that half hour, so it will sit between two numbers.
facts: At 3:30 the minute hand points to six. The hour hand is halfway between three and four.

title: How can you tell how much time has passed?
answer: Elapsed time is how long something lasts from start to finish. Suppose you begin reading at 2:45 and stop at 3:20. Count fifteen minutes from 2:45 to 3:00. Then count the twenty minutes from 3:00 to 3:20. Add those two jumps to find that you read for thirty-five minutes. Splitting the time at a full hour can be easier than comparing the two clock numbers directly.
facts: An hour lasts sixty minutes, so moving forward thirty minutes also moves forward half an hour.

title: How can stacks of dots show measurements?
answer: A dot plot can show measurements along a marked number line. Place one dot above the right number for each measurement. If two leaves are both four centimeters long, put two dots in a stack above four. The tallest stack shows a length that appeared a lot in your collection. A dot alone farther down the line might come from a much longer leaf. You can still see which measurements appeared and how often.
facts: One dot usually represents one observation in this kind of plot.
